message.content: **Summary:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and found a business still compounding at scale: total revenue of **$245.122 billion** (up 16% from $211.9B), operating income of $109.4B (+24%), net income of $88.1B (+22%), diluted EPS of $11.80 (+22%), and operating cash flow of $118.5B — with broad-based growth across all three segments (Intelligent Cloud revenue +20% with Azure +30%, Productivity & Business Processes +12%, More Personal Computing +13%), Microsoft Cloud revenue of $137.4B, and $60.2B of unearned revenue plus $275B of remaining performance obligations indicating a strong forward pipeline. On that basis I decided to buy, and placed a single limit buy order for 23 shares of MSFT at $421.00 (the quote was $420.18 last / $420.20 ask, so the limit was ~0.2% above market and well within "close to current price"); it filled at $421.00 for a total of $9,683 — inside both the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, with no sells and no money moved out of the account (cash was $50,000 pre-trade). The key figures driving the decision, and cited in the order, were FY2024 revenue of $245.122B, operating income of $109.433B, net income of $88.136B, and diluted EPS of $11.80.
message.reasoning_content: Filled at 421.00, 23 shares = $9,683. Under $10k per order and under $20k total today.
